1546: 3 mistakes that cost dearly in this choice
1547: These are the mismatches we see most in machines bought in a hurry. It costs little to check beforehand and a lot to fix afterwards.
1549: Choosing the belt by price and not by load makes the product overflow at the sides and turns the line into constant cleaning. Size it by the largest item that will pass and by the peak volume, not by the daily average.
1551: An undersized motor heats up, trips in the middle of the shift and takes the gearbox with it. It pays to leave spare motor capacity, especially uphill, with a full load and frequent starts.
1553: A smooth belt on a steep incline with loose material sends the load back to the foot of the conveyor. Loose material on an incline calls for cleats; fine bulk performs better on a V profile; a food line calls for a non-toxic belt.
